Its test serializer and 1,726-case claim are supplementary, not the pinned Athena oracle. Run the existing 57-file/1,733-document WPT corpus on identical UTF-8 bytes; compare tree and parse-error annotations to WPT, and separately record legacy parse_warnings, projection/locator/table/AAE output and enforceable resource-bound plus IPC cost before any performance matrix. Keep `astral-html` 0.0.4 Reader/Document as a separate source-order extraction architecture candidate because its docs state it does not implement browser tree construction, MathML or namespace adjustments; it cannot replace repaired-DOM output or warning counts unless it passes the same consumer gold. Do not label `tl`, `html5gum`, or `lol_html` as equivalent full-DOM comparators: upstream documents non-WHATWG gaps, tokenizer-only/tree-builder integration, and streaming rewriting respectively. Any fast-path capability with different semantics must be versioned and independently quality-gated. The published `html5-parser` API exposes no warning-count field or per-document budget; if used without a reviewed fork, a second warning pass and external resource controls are part of the candidate cost and containment. Any mismatch against the pinned Rust parser blocks same-contract semantic admission; masking the AAE field or labeling a parser-specific difference does not satisfy this gate. A per-tag cap is a separate rejection-policy change. Compare complete parse-to-consumer cost and failure ownership against independent gold on Linux. Record that Lexbor's public allocator hook is process-wide; if a hard allocation quota is required, prove a concurrency-safe allocator policy or use an OS-limited worker and include its process and IPC costs.
language_panels.evidence_basis: The selected compatibility contract requires exact Rust parse_warnings parity for identical UTF-8 bytes. A previous single-parser adapter revision characterized six HTML cases and failed strict AAE parity on table foster parenting (5 Rust vs 2 Lexbor) and duplicate attributes (3 vs 1). The current research candidate calls the feature-gated bounded html5ever warning counter, drops its tree, then parses with Lexbor and serializes the Rust count; this adds a second full parser pass rather than mapping Lexbor diagnostics. The strict six-case adapter suite passes on Windows x64 using reused pinned Lexbor v3.0.0 and C-shim artifacts; Rust/Cargo 1.99.1 compiled the changed core and adapter and all six tests passed, and adapter Clippy passed with warnings denied. This verifies the Windows FFI/output path against the cached native build, not a clean C rebuild. The current host lacks CMake/C compiler and WSL2 is unavailable; Linux ABI, resource bounds and performance remain NOT VERIFIED. Literal chunk/output, resource rejection and table behavior are also checked. Source review shows html5ever sends tokenizer/tree-builder parse errors to the same sink callback counter, while Lexbor stores typed tree errors (ID plus token byte range) and a separate tokenizer error array; the opt-in trace records source, IDs and byte ranges with a 256-event cap; a 300-error boundary test preserves aggregate counts. Lexbor emits tree IDs 4 and 29 for the table fixture while Rust reports five callbacks, and only tree ID 4 for duplicate attributes while Rust reports three. The pinned document setup enables duplicate retention, skipping Lexbor tokenizer duplicate-error recording, so raw array totals are not a direct Rust-warning translation; no general mapping has been established. This is not a native/2 executor or Linux result. The adapter counts/rejects parser nodes while walking the already-built tree, so it does not cap Lexbor parse allocations. At the pinned commit, the parser accepts UTF-8 input and exposes tokenizer errors separately; POSIX allocator callbacks are file-static and changed without synchronization, with no per-document allocator context. Official-source candidate audit dated 2026-10-25: crates.io html5-parser 0.1.0 is MIT and its published Cargo.toml has no runtime dependencies, but it declares no rust-version, disables automatic tests, excludes tests/ from the package, and docs.rs built it with rustc 1.100.0-nightly; GitHub's README claims 1,726/1,726 applicable tree cases, which needs a pinned source/test receipt and stable 1.99.1 verification. Its public `parse` API returns a `Document` without a documented parse-warning/error field, so exact Athena warning-count parity is unresolved and any second pass or maintained fork must be charged to full-path results. The corrected 2026-10-25 bounded runtime probe executed `html5-parser 0.4.0` on six existing warning-oracle cases: its exposed error counts `(0,10,2,0,0,2)` matched Athena warning counts `(1,5,3,1,1,4)` on 0/6; no warning-mapping adapter or full WPT comparison is verified. The 2026-10-25 exact-version follow-up reviewed `html5-parser 0.4.0` source, which does expose ordered tokenizer/tree parse errors and includes processing-instruction token states; this creates a narrow local standards-conformance screen, not evidence of parity, bounded allocation, performance, or adoption. The local WPT `processing-instructions.dat` Git blob matches current upstream blob `c516eab0943042edb5cca8562c4087329843814b`; WHATWG PR #12118 and WPT commit cf0642a are the primary change/test references. The report-only Rust run executed 1,733 whole-document cases and found 105 tree mismatches/482 warning-annotation deltas; only the 83 PI-related mismatches are attributed to that standards change. The exact Rust warning-counter test passed its literal 5/3 expectations. The candidate public API has no scripting option while Athena defaults scripting on; the local WPT set has 10 script-off and 8 script-on markers. Its upstream conformance harness has a `HTML5LIB_BLESS=1` path that rewrites the expected-failure file; keep it unset and hash inputs before and after. The unmodified candidate is therefore a gated standards-upgrade study, not a same-contract drop-in. Sources: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12118 ; https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/commit/cf0642a4d2a851574afd696f566987f84f92849f ; https://docs.rs/html5-parser/0.4.0/. astral-html 0.0.4 is MIT OR Apache-2.0, declares MSRV 1.97 and one memchr runtime dependency, and its versioned docs explicitly state that it does not do browser tree construction, MathML or namespace adjustments; its published microbench table is upstream-only and is not campaign evidence. The muskitty-html5-parser 0.2.1 docs.rs page reports 7,022/7,036 tokenizer and 1,716/1,716 tree cases, while the current repository README says 0.2.3 and different perfect totals; keep it out of the frozen matrix until exact release/source/test provenance is resolved. html5gum 0.8.4 documents a tokenizer API and an experimental html5ever/scraper tree-builder integration; lol_html documents a streaming rewriter. These are architecture/attribution leads, not performance or adoption findings. Enforce egress outside the browser across all descendants; verify denied DNS/private/metadata targets, redirects, subresources, workers/service workers, WebSockets, cancellation and process exit. On GCE, do not rely on VPC firewall for metadata or loopback: isolate browser/driver at a guest-OS process boundary and keep all secret material out of their environment. Prefer no VM service account when controller work does not need GCP identity; if Secret Manager access is required, grant a controller identity `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` only on the exact required secret, never project-wide, and block the browser/driver identity from metadata. Probe IPv4 metadata and IPv6 only where the target VM supports it; record IPv6 capability explicitly, and classify an unavailable IPv6 endpoint as NOT_APPLICABLE rather than proof of firewall denial. language_panels.evidence_basis: Current isolated candidates are `thirtyfour 0.38.1` (MSRV 1.88, MIT OR Apache-2.0) and `selenium-webdriver 4.51.0` (Node >=22, Apache-2.0), which can use one W3C ChromeDriver/browser pair. Local Rust 1.99.1 and Node 22.21.1 meet declared minimums; no SDK is installed and no browser/driver executable was found on PATH in the local check. The target-cloud Node runtime is NOT VERIFIED. Google documents ChromeDriver as W3C WebDriver/WebDriver BiDi and recommends Chrome-for-Testing matched binaries; raw CDP has no public API/backward-compatibility guarantee. Playwright route hooks miss Service-Worker-handled requests, so browser interception cannot be the SSRF/egress control. GCP VPC firewall rules do not apply to metadata-server or loopback traffic; untrusted processes must be sandboxed. A GCE service account exposes metadata credentials to any process that can query the metadata service; Secret Manager documents `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` can be granted at the individual-secret resource level. No implementation, integration or performance result exists. language_panels.evidence_basis: Official current release candidates are rmcp 3.7.0 (released 2026-10-22, Apache-2.0, MSRV 1.88) and @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.4.0 (released 2026-10-23, Apache-2.0); both implement the stable 2026-07-28 MCP spec. The local Rust 1.99.1 and Node 22.21.1 runtimes satisfy their documented minimums. Both SDKs are pinned and exercised by an isolated local fixture: the Rust adapter built, and the TypeScript packages were installed with scripts disabled. The isolated fixture now invokes the same compiled Athena core_probe from both SDK servers and checks AAE output parity over local stdio and stateless HTTP. This is synthetic wrapper-to-core preflight; the target-cloud Node runtime remains NOT VERIFIED. TypeScript SDK v2 moves server-side OAuth/auth out of its core server package while rmcp has optional auth features, so SDK-native auth asymmetry cannot be folded into a language-speed claim. The current spec removes protocol-level HTTP sessions; prior 19.15 session wording is superseded for the primary panel. Local protocol/build and synthetic Rust-core wiring preflights are recorded. Both SDKs now use bounded stdout capture, strict UTF-8/newline validation, completed tool-error results, awaited ordinary direct-child cleanup, SSE progress streaming, caller-disconnect child cancellation, and non-blocking concurrent child-probe admission (ATHENA_MCP_MAX_INFLIGHT in 1..=8, default 2, rejecting saturation before spawn with CORE_PROBE_ADMISSION_SATURATED and holding permits until child exit); a Windows preflight exercised four valid SDK/transport combinations plus 22 controlled producer-failure, caller-disconnect, admission-saturation, and sibling-disconnect-isolation controls. Real-agent tasks, proxy/network-blackhole cancellation, repeated performance and cloud-runtime results remain NOT VERIFIED. These versions are isolated research candidates, not approved production dependencies. Sources: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk/releases/tag/rmcp-v3.7.0 ; https://crates.io/crates/rmcp/3.7.0 ; https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol/server%402.4.0 ; https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modelcontextprotocol/server/v/2.4.0 ; https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/327243ce/docs/migration.md ; https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http Exact 2026-10-25 tag-source review found TypeScript v2.4.0's direct McpServer-to-StdioServerTransport entry serves only the 2025 era; modern stdio uses serveStdio and strict modern-only requires legacy reject. createMcpHandler supports modern HTTP per request but defaults to stateless legacy fallback. RMCP 3.7.0 defaults supported_protocol_versions to all known versions; its HTTP config defaults legacy_session_mode=true and stateless_protocol_metadata_required=false, so the panel must explicitly pin the modern contract. The isolated fixture runs the same native Rust task search candidate retriever, task/source/revision resolver, and compact handle verifier (athena_search_task, athena_extract_document, and athena_expand_handle -> core_probe task-search, task-export, and task-expand) through both SDKs over stdio and stateless HTTP, executes the existing W2 synthetic consumer for all 16 task inputs in full and compact form (128/128 contracts satisfied, including 16/16 F04 HTML-table contracts and native/SDK search candidate retrieval for all query tasks), and passes 76 direct cross-tenant/task/source/revision, tampered-handle, wrong-query, unsearchable-task, caller-scope-override, and unusable-evidence controls with independent fact/table scoring and SDK evidence/answer parity. Workflow orchestration and scoring remain Python-side; live user-facing integration, production IAM, proxy/network cancellation, repeated cost and target-cloud evidence are still NOT VERIFIED. This remains a functional synthetic preflight, not a performance decision.
